device.name: TrackerLab Unitree G1 23-DoF motion tracking (Isaac Lab simulation)

facts.text: TrackerLab-Tracking-Unitree-G1-23D-Walk is registered with entry point trackerLab.tracker_env:ManagerBasedTrackerEnv and the training config g1_23d_tracking_env_cfg:G1TrackingWalk
ManagerBasedTrackerEnv extends ManagerBasedRLEnv and its constructor takes cfg, an optional render_mode and keyword arguments
step(action) calls the parent step, updates the motion manager and returns the observation, reward, terminated, timeout and extras buffers
reset(seed, env_ids, options) forwards to the parent reset and returns the observation buffer and extras
The action configuration is a joint-position action over all robot joints with scale 0.5, the default joint offset and a configured clip of -6.0 to 6.0
The G1 23-DoF tracking task selects the 23-joint motion alignment, sets the action scale to 0.5, enables a 5-step policy observation history and sets the episode length to 20.0 s
G1_23D_MOTION_ALIGN_CFG lists 23 gym joint names for the G1 23-DoF tracking task

The policy observation group is the dof-position command, root-velocity command, base linear velocity, base angular velocity, projected gravity, relative joint position, relative joint velocity and last action
set_no_scanner removes the height scanner and the height_scan policy observation
The G1 23-DoF tracking task calls set_no_scanner
The base configuration uses 4 physics steps of 0.005 s per environment step
The G1 23-DoF tracking task sets the episode length to 20.0 s and disables the base-contact termination
The termination terms are a base height below 0.2 m and a bad orientation beyond 0.8 rad
The reset events sample base pose x and y in -2.5 to 2.5, yaw in -3.14 to 3.14, base velocity x, y and z in -1.0 to 1.0, roll, pitch and yaw in -0.5 to 0.5 and the joint velocity scale in -1.0 to 1.0
The environment config sets sim.physx.gpu_max_rigid_patch_count to 10 * 2**15
TrackerLab extends IsaacLab and requires IsaacLab and its dependencies to be installed
The setup guide includes Isaac Sim installation and Python environment setup

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 reseeds Python's random.Random, and the analytic update is deterministic, so one seed repeats a trajectory; the upstream Isaac Lab reset uses its own random generators and domain randomisation, and the two were not compared

gaps: analytic F0 stand-in: no Isaac Sim or PhysX, no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor, terrain, noise or rendering model; the fake sets relative joint positions from an approximate zero-offset target, reports reward 0 and never terminates on height, orientation or contact. The upstream config enables default joint offsets; its processing implementation is outside the clone

the raw action space is built by Isaac Lab's action manager outside the clone and was not observed here; the fake exposes an unbounded Box of 23 action values, so action.values is operator_required at the endpoint. site-limits.example.json supplies illustrative fake bounds only; the configured clip of -6.0 to 6.0 does not establish a raw action-space bound

the fake returns the policy observation group as one 104-value vector (23 dof-position command, 3 root-velocity command, 3 base linear velocity, 3 base angular velocity, 3 projected gravity, 23 relative joint positions, 23 relative joint velocities and 23 last actions); the upstream group is assembled by Isaac Lab and the task enables a 5-step history (g1_23d_tracking_env_cfg.py:183), so the real flattened observation is larger and its exact shape was not observed

the fake applies the task's angular-velocity observation scale 0.25 and joint-velocity observation scale 0.05 in its analytic observations (g1_23d_tracking_env_cfg.py:174-179); initial joint velocities remain independent placeholder samples, not the upstream reset_joints_by_scale result

the upstream environment is vectorised over 4096 environments (g1_23d_tracking_env_cfg.py:163) and returns torch tensors; the MHS Gymnasium bridge drives one environment and the fake uses Python lists

the fake does not model the termination terms (base height below 0.2 m and bad orientation beyond 0.8 rad, tracking_humanoid_env_cfg.py:20-21) or any reward term; its own episode budget is 1000 control steps and it does not model Isaac Lab's in-step episode resets

the upstream stack (Isaac Lab, Isaac Sim, PhysX, torch and a GPU) was not installed or run where the gate runs; only fake is declared. The generic gymnasium.make fallback is not a supported live adapter: the upstream constructor requires cfg (manager_based_tracker_env.py:11), and the scripts bootstrap AppLauncher, import task registrations and parse cfg before gym.make. The native returns vectorised torch buffers; no torch/batch conversion or application lifecycle adapter is provided
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and clock lockstep; 20.0 ms is one environment control step (4 physics steps of 0.005 s, tracking_env_base.py:40-43), not an integration performed by the fake
no rendering, video, checkpoint or exact snapshot/restore is offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state and the fake has none

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: The raw action space has no verified finite bound in this clone; bound all 23 raw values for the deployment. The configured processed-target clip is not an input envelope; site-limits.example.json contains illustrative fake data only

safe_state.description: the declared analytic fake stops advancing and retains its cached observation, target, tick and episode; no step or world reset is accepted while latched. mhs.safety.reset releases only the latch and advances no ticks. No pause or stop of an external Isaac Sim application is provided; a live adapter is outside this package
